question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=3x(t)-6y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=x(t)-2y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following gives all equilibrium points of the system of linear differential equations above?
question.worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]x(t),
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

The equilibrium (fixed) points of a system ${x}^{′}(t)=f(x,y)$ are the points for which $f(x,y)=0.$ So, we get the following system of linear equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}3x-6y=0 \\ x-2y=0\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the first equation is a multiple of the second one:

$$
3(x-2y)=3x-6y,
$$

so we can disregard the first equation.

From the second equation, we get

$$
x-2y=0\,⇒\,x=2y.
$$

Therefore, the equilibrium points are given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2k \\ k\end{aligned}],\,k\in R.
$$
